marks.gloss_en: כמאן? כרבי מאיר, דתנן ... וחכמים אומרים עד שיטביל את כולו -- whose view is this? R' Meir's, in the Mikvaot mishna, where the Sages say: until he immerses all of it
all handles of vessels that are long and which he will cut down -- he immerses up to the place of the measure; the words of R' Meir
אפילו תימא רבנן, חיבורי אוכלין כמאן דמפרתי דמי ונגיעי בהדדי -- even the Rabbis hold that connections of foods count as separated and touching
you may even say the Rabbis: connections of foods are as if separated, and they touch one another
and the Sages say: not until he immerses all of it
טרפה תוכיח, ששחיטתה מטהרתה מידי נבלה ואינה מתירתה באכילה -- as the tereifa's slaughter purifies it without permitting it, so the mother's slaughter purifies the limb
מאי קאמר? -- 'it protects what is not her body more' does not answer 'if so, let it permit it for eating'
חסורי מחסרא והכי קתני -- the baraita is lacking the Sages' טרפה תוכיח and R' Meir's reply (= p_rava_chasurei_mechasra)
טרפה תוכיח -- the tereifa's slaughter purifies it and does not permit it for eating (= p_tereifa_shechita_metaheret_velo_matira; the binyan_av m_tereifa_tochiach_73a)

Rava: the baraita is lacking, and this is what it teaches: R' Meir's 'if so, permit it' is answered by 'let the tereifa prove it', and 'it protects what is not her body more' answers his further reply
R' Meir: לא, אם טיהרה שחיטת טרפה אותה, דבר שהיא גופה, תטהר את האבר דבר שאינו גופה? (baraita B, 73a.13: אותה ואת האבר המדולדל בה... תטהר את העובר)
הרבה מצלת על שאינו גופה יותר מגופה, שהרי שנינו: חותך מן העובר שבמעיה מותר באכילה, מן הטחול ומן הכליות אסור באכילה (= p_harbe_matzelet; again at 73a.14)
שהרי שנינו: חותך מן העובר שבמעיה מותר באכילה, מן הטחול ומן הכליות אסור באכילה -- the mother's slaughter permits the fetus's pieces but not her own organs' (no SupportKind names a mishna citation)
the Sages: [slaughter] protects what is not her body more than [it protects] her body
תניא נמי הכי -- baraita B carries the Sages' טרפה תוכיח that Rava restores
baraita B: R' Meir: who purified this limb? they: its mother's slaughter. [he:] if so, permit it for eating! they: let the tereifa prove it...
אם כן תתירנו באכילה! -- if the mother's slaughter purifies the limb, it should also permit it for eating

baraita A as cited: R' Meir: who purified this limb from carcass impurity? its mother's slaughter! if so, let it permit it for eating! they said: [slaughter] protects what is not her body more than her body
מיתיבי: R' Meir in the baraita grants that slaughter purifies the hanging limb -- yet by Reish Lakish he disputes it
מיתיבי: R' Meir in the baraita grants that slaughter purifies the hanging limb -- yet by R' Yochanan all agree slaughter makes it fallen. אלא לרבי יוחנן קשיא (73b.2)
[R' Meir in baraita B:] the tereifa's slaughter purifies her and the limb hanging from her -- what is her body
Reish Lakish: as the dispute [of R' Meir and the Sages] in fetuses, so is the dispute in [hanging] limbs
R' Yochanan: the dispute is in the limb of a fetus
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina: R' Yochanan's reason for the Sages -- this [fetus's limb] has a remedy by return, and that [hanging limb] has no remedy by return
כדאבוה דשמואל -- the Sages' 'contact with a slaughtered tereifa' stands on Shmuel's father's ruling that a slaughtered tereifa conveys impurity to sacred food
טרפה שחוטה מי מטמיא? -- does a slaughtered tereifa convey impurity [that its contact should be impure]?
אין, כדאבוה דשמואל -- yes, as Shmuel's father said: a tereifa that one slaughtered conveys impurity to sacred food
Shmuel's father: a tereifa that one slaughtered conveys impurity to sacred food
